cityQuoteAttribution: A Riga legend: a spirit rises from the Daugava every hundred years to ask whether the city is finished. If anyone says yes, Riga will sink.
heroTitle: Riga hero — Diego Delso (CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons)
wordsPreamble:
- Latvian is one of only two living Baltic languages. Its closest relative is Lithuanian, not Estonian or Russian.
- Stress almost always falls on the first syllable. A line over a vowel (ā, ē, ī, ū) means it is long.
- About a third of Riga’s people speak Russian at home. English is widely spoken by younger people.
- The city is Rīga in Latvian, said REE-gah.
